payload.title: nats_credential_set_outside_auth_mode_branch recognises only a plain `=` assignment to options.user/pass/token, so ??=, ||=, object-literal or spread properties, Object.assign and computed-key writes in the factory module are never reported
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:741-752 (credentialFieldWritten returns a field only for a BinaryExpression with EqualsToken whose left side is a property access or a string-literal element access)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:690-707 (the SET rule reports only the nodes credentialFieldWritten accepts, so every other write form is silent)

tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.nats.test.ts:79-107 (the pinned variants are `=` writes, an if chain, a switch and near-misses; no ??=, literal, spread or Object.assign variant is pinned)
libs/backend-common/src/nats/nats-connection.factory.ts:285-291 (the compliant factory writes options.token/user/pass with `=` inside branches on authMode, the only shape the rule reads)
payload.rule_violated: ADR-015 (cert-is-identity): under mTLS no user, pass or token may reach the CONNECT frame; CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 3 (make it detectable) requires the detector to catch every spelling of the violation, not one.
payload.notes: A change to buildNatsConnectionOptions that writes the credentials with `options.token ??= authToken;`, `Object.assign(options, { pass: authPass });`, `return { ...options, user: authUser };` or `options[key] = authPass` outside any authMode branch produces zero nats_credential_set_outside_auth_mode_branch findings. The same patch written as `options.token = authToken;` is a HIGH finding (pinned by the 'no guard at all' variant), so the rule fires on one spelling of a violation and is silent on the others. Reproduced by running the functions at lines 666-828 of the adapter on a factory containing each shape: ??=, ||=, +=, object literal, spread, Object.assign, destructuring assignment and a computed key all returned no finding. The dynamic spec nats-connection.factory.auth.spec.ts is the only other line of defence for the factory. Close condition: Make the write detector recognise every assignment operator (=, ??=, ||=, &&=), object-literal and spread properties named after the credential fields, Object.assign sources, and non-literal element keys on the options object, and add one variant per shape to security-boundary-adapter.nats.test.ts, each expected to produce a finding at its row, while the six existing variants and the real-factory clean pin stay green. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 1). Verified at head a47dc4d57c of open pull request #2134; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
